section_summary: This section covers diplomatic reporting, intelligence despatches, and State Department analyses from January through October 1940 concerning the reorganization of the Japanese Government, beginning with the installation of the moderate Yonai Cabinet and its subsequent collapse under Army pressure in July 1940. It documents the emergence of the Second Konoye Cabinet, the formulation of its totalitarian 'new political structure' (Shintaisei), the creation of a centralized Cabinet Intelligence Bureau with enhanced press censorship, and Japan's strategic shift toward closer alignment with the European Axis powers. The files also incorporate international and regional viewpoints from Hong Kong and Chungking analyzing Japan's economic difficulties, the expiration of the 1911 U.S.-Japanese commercial treaty, and the military impasse of the 'China Incident'.

subfiles.about: Analysis of the designation of Admiral Mitsumasa Yonai as Premier of Japan and its anticipated effect on army factions and foreign relations.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memorandum on Admiral Yonai as Premier, chosen to reconcile military differences over China; moderate and opposed to the Axis alliance, his cabinet will keep communication with the United States open.
subfiles.title: Designation of Admiral Yonai as Premier of Japan

subfiles.about: Record of tracking a sealed letter from the White House addressed to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew for dispatch via diplomatic pouch.
subfiles.from: Office of Adviser on Political Relations (Stanley K. Hornbeck)
subfiles.summary: Memorandum confirming a White House letter to Ambassador Grew arrived February 14 and went to the mail room for pouch.
subfiles.title: Delivery of White House Letter to Ambassador Grew

subfiles.about: President Roosevelt requests Secretary Hull to read Ambassador Grew's letter and prepare a draft reply.
subfiles.summary: Roosevelt asks Hull to draft a reply to Ambassador Grew's enclosed communication for his signature; routed to Far Eastern Affairs and Hornbeck.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Secretary of State Requesting Draft Reply to Ambassador Grew

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew shares his assessment of Admiral Yonai's appointment as Prime Minister and Arita as Foreign Minister.
subfiles.summary: Grew writes informally to Roosevelt approving Yonai's selection as Prime Minister, expecting no radical China policy change but possible easing of discrimination against American interests, and noting his friendship with Arita.
subfiles.title: Letter from Ambassador Grew to President Roosevelt on the Yonai Cabinet

subfiles.about: Secretary Hull submits a draft reply to Ambassador Grew's letter of January 16 for the President's approval.
subfiles.summary: Hull sends Roosevelt a draft reply to Grew's letter on the new Japanese cabinet, to be returned for transmission by pouch.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the President Submitting Draft Reply to Ambassador Grew

subfiles.about: Draft reply from President Roosevelt acknowledging Ambassador Grew's observations on the Yonai and Arita appointments.
subfiles.summary: Draft letter from Roosevelt to Grew thanking him for comments on Prime Minister Yonai and Foreign Minister Arita.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter from President Roosevelt to Ambassador Grew

subfiles.about: Internal State Department note conveying Secretary Hull's request for a draft of the President's reply to Grew.
subfiles.from: Office of the Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Routing slip instructing Hornbeck to prepare Roosevelt's draft reply to Grew.
subfiles.title: Routing Note Requesting Draft Reply to Ambassador Grew

subfiles.about: Report on Hong Kong press reaction to the new Yonai Cabinet and the impending expiration of the 1911 commercial treaty.
subfiles.from: Addison E. Southard (American Consul General, Hong Kong)
subfiles.summary: Consul General Southard transmits a South China Morning Post editorial on the new Yonai Cabinet, backing a firm U.S. stance after denunciation of the 1911 commercial treaty.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 595: Hong Kong Press Comments on New Japanese Cabinet and Considers Denounced American-Japanese Treaty as its First Problem

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 4485 on the fall of the Abe Cabinet and the establishment of the Yonai Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 4485 (February 13, 1940): resignation of the Abe Cabinet and inauguration of the Yonai Cabinet.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Resignation of the Abe Cabinet and Inauguration of the Yonai Cabinet

subfiles.about: Detailed diplomatic report recounting the resignation of the Abe Cabinet, the Imperial command to Admiral Yonai, and the organization of the new ministry.
subfiles.summary: Report No. 146 extract: the Abe Cabinet resigned en bloc after losing military support; Yonai was chosen as a moderate compromise, with his cabinet listed and his three-part policy statement.
subfiles.title: Report on Internal Political Conditions: Resignation of the Abe Cabinet and Inauguration of the Yonai Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Despatch No. 4486 concerning the selection of Admiral Yonai and the policies of his cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 4486 (February 13, 1940): Abe Cabinet's resignation and the Yonai Cabinet's composition and policies.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Resignation of the Abe Cabinet and Selection of Admiral Yonai

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 486 regarding reports that Prince Konoe will resign from the Privy Council.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 486 (June 23, 1940): Konoe reported to resign as Privy Council President, replaced by Hiranuma.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Konoe Reported to Resign as President of Privy Council

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports Japanese press statements forecasting the resignation of Prince Konoe from the Privy Council.
subfiles.summary: A brief telegram from Tokyo stating that the morning press reported Prince Fumimaro Konoe's impending resignation as President of the Privy Council within the next few days. The report further indicates that former Premier Kiichiro Hiranuma is scheduled to succeed Konoe in the post.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 486: Reported Resignation of Konoe from Privy Council

subfiles.about: Report on the inaugural meeting and structure of the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau and tightening censorship of the press.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports a centralized Cabinet Intelligence Bureau merging service and ministry intelligence functions, ending separate press conferences for foreign correspondents and tightening censorship, including bans on political forecasts and on reporting talks with seven nations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 723: Organization of the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau and Vernacular Press Censorship

subfiles.about: Analytical memorandum assessing the personnel, policy makers, and political orientation of the newly formed Second Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Ivan B. White (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memorandum on Konoe's new cabinet, profiling Tojo, Yoshida, Matsuoka and Hoshino and their Kwantung Army and Manchukuo links; it expects an aggressive pro-Axis policy and a stiffer attitude toward the United States.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on the New Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 651 concerning Chuichi Ohashi's appointment as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 651 (August 2, 1940): Ohashi, former Manchukuo counselor, succeeds Tani as Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Appointment of Chuichi Ohashi as Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports the official announcement naming Chuichi Ohashi as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.summary: A telegraphic message confirming Japanese press reports that Chuichi Ohashi, recently Counselor to the Manchukuo Government, has been appointed Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs in succession to Masayuki Tani.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 651: Appointment of Chuichi Ohashi as Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: Memorandum summarizing Tokyo Despatch No. 4900 on the fall of the Yonai Cabinet and the creation of the Second Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memorandum on Despatch No. 4900: after German victories opinion shifted to opportunism and Axis alignment; the Jushin chose Konoe, and the military character of the new government is a setback for American-Japanese relations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 4900 Regarding the Fall of the Yonai Cabinet and Formation of the Second Konoye Cabinet

subfiles.about: Comprehensive despatch detailing the political crisis that brought down the Yonai Cabinet and the installation of the Second Konoye Cabinet, with policy declarations.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew provides an extensive review of the fall of the Yonai Cabinet, engineered by War Minister Hata and Army leaders dissatisfied with Yonai's resistance to an Axis alliance and hesitation toward the new single-party structure. He examines the selection of Prince Konoe by the Jushin conference and details the formation of an inner cabinet dominated by Tojo, Matsuoka, and Yoshida. Enclosed with the despatch are official English translations of the Japanese Government's statement of Fundamental National Policies of August 1, 1940, and Foreign Minister Matsuoka's declaration regarding the Imperial Way (Kodo) and Greater East Asian coprosperity.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 4900: Fall of the Yonai Cabinet and Formation of the Second Konoye Cabinet

subfiles.about: Summary of Mukden Despatch No. 465 regarding Naoki Hoshino's transition from Manchukuo's General Affairs Board to the Tokyo Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memorandum on Mukden Despatch No. 465: Naoki Hoshino, de facto chief administrator of Manchukuo since 1937, enters the Cabinet.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Mukden Despatch No. 465 Regarding Entry of Naoki Hoshino into Cabinet

subfiles.about: Report on Naoki Hoshino's resignation from Manchukuo to join the Konoe Cabinet and the succession of Rokuzo Takebe.
subfiles.from: J. Graham Parsons (American Vice Consul, Mukden)
subfiles.summary: Vice Consul Parsons reports Hoshino left Manchukuo's General Affairs Board to join the Tokyo Cabinet, succeeded by Rokuzo Takebe, giving unprecedented integration between Tokyo and Manchuria.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 465: Resignation and Entry into the Japanese Cabinet of Mr. Naoki Hoshino; Appointment of Mr. Rokuzo Takebe

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports the sudden hospitalization of Navy Minister Zengo Yoshida and rumors of his replacement.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Navy Minister Yoshida hospitalized with serious illness, prompting resignation rumors; the Naval Attaché confirmed it, and Grew asks the Navy Department be alerted.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 790: Hospitalization of Navy Minister Admiral Yoshida

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 489 on Prince Konoe's resignation from the Privy Council and his replacement.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 489 (June 24, 1940): Konoe's resignation as Privy Council President, succeeded by Ishihara (Ichihara in record).
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Resignation of Prince Konoye as President of the Privy Council

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 528 forecasting cabinet changes and Konoe's return as Prime Minister.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 528 (July 2, 1940): Konoe emerging as likely next Prime Minister.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Possible Changes in Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 585 reporting the resignation en bloc of the entire Yonai Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 585 (July 16, 1940): the Yonai Cabinet resigned en bloc.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Resignation en Bloc of Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 580 on the press reactions to the cabinet resignation and Konoe's candidacy.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 580 (July 17, 1940): press comment on the cabinet's fall, with Konoe expected to form the next government.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Press Reports on Resignation of Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew details the collapse of the Yonai Cabinet following War Minister Hata's resignation and Konoe's impending appointment.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the Yonai Cabinet fell over Army-Premier differences on diplomatic renovation and internal structure, after War Minister Hata demanded resignation and named no successor; Konoe is expected to form a government.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 580: Sequence of Events in the Resignation of the Yonai Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 613 on foreign policy formulation and the conservative complexion of the Konoe Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 613 (July 23, 1940): Konoe Cabinet's foreign policy formulation and Yonai's retirement; ministry conservative.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Formulation of Foreign Policy by Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 611 announcing the formal investiture of the Second Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 611 (July 23, 1940): Konoe's cabinet formally invested the previous evening.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Formal Investiture of Konoye Cabinet

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew confirms the Imperial investiture of the Second Konoye Cabinet and Matsuoka's concurrent appointment.
subfiles.summary: A concise telegram confirming that Prince Konoe's cabinet was formally invested on the evening of July 22, 1940. It confirms the cabinet roster previously reported and notes that Foreign Minister Yosuke Matsuoka is serving concurrently as Minister for Overseas Affairs.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 611: Formal Investiture of the Konoye Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 617 on the resignation of Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs Masayuki Tani.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 617 (July 25, 1940): press reports Tani's resignation as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Resignation of Vice Minister Masayuki Tani

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports the resignation of Masayuki Tani as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.summary: A brief telegram reporting that the Tokyo press published notice of the resignation of Masayuki Tani from his post as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs following the installation of Foreign Minister Matsuoka.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 617: Resignation of Vice Minister Masayuki Tani

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 746 regarding Matsuoka's statements to Ambassador Steinhardt about controlling the Army.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 746 (August 26, 1940): Matsuoka tells Steinhardt Konoe promised to stay ten years and they expect to control the Army.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Matsuoka Remarks to Ambassador Steinhardt

subfiles.about: Duplicate cross-reference sheets indexing Vichy Telegram No. 125 reporting Ambassador Sawada's satisfaction with Matsuoka's appointment.
subfiles.summary: Two duplicate cross-reference sheets referencing Telegram No. 125 sent from Vichy by Robert D. Murphy on July 21, 1940. The report notes that Japanese Ambassador Sawada expressed satisfaction over the appointment of Yosuke Matsuoka as Foreign Minister, filed under decimal file 851.00/2038.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Japanese Ambassador Sawada's Reaction to Matsuoka Appointment

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew transmits the full membership list and career sketches of the newly formed Second Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Grew gives the incoming Konoe Cabinet roster of eleven ministers with backgrounds, including Matsuoka, Tojo, Yoshida, Kawada and Hoshino, noting many business executives and former Manchukuo administrators.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 608: Lineup of the Second Konoye Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 800 on the appointment of Admiral Koshiro Oikawa as Navy Minister.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 800 (September 5, 1940): Admiral Oikawa (recorded as Mikawa) appointed Navy Minister after Yoshida's resignation.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Appointment of Admiral Oikawa as Navy Minister

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports the appointment of Admiral Koshiro Oikawa as Navy Minister succeeding the ailing Admiral Yoshida.
subfiles.summary: Official announcement that Admiral Koshiro Oikawa (transcribed Mikawa), formerly Yokosuka commander, succeeds Admiral Yoshida, who resigned from ill health, as Navy Minister.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 800: Appointment of Admiral Oikawa as Navy Minister

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Tokyo Telegram No. 853 reporting a press ban on speculative accounts of extraordinary cabinet meetings.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 853 (September 17, 1940): press ban on speculation about extraordinary Cabinet meetings.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Press Ban on Speculative Cabinet Commentary

subfiles.about: Summary of Chungking Despatch No. 655 analyzing Chinese press commentary on Prince Konoe's return to premiership.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memorandum on Chungking Despatch No. 655: a Central Daily News editorial says Konoe's administration can neither end the China conflict nor realize South Seas expansion.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Chungking Despatch No. 655: Chinese Comment on Konoe's Return

subfiles.about: Ambassador Johnson transmits and discusses a Chinese editorial analyzing Konoe's strategic dilemma in China and the South Seas.
subfiles.summary: Johnson transmits a Central Daily News editorial: Chinese officials believe Konoe's new structure cannot end the China war or enable southward expansion, and predict the cabinet's fall and military dictatorship.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 655: Chinese Comment on the Return of Prince Konoye to Power: Present Situation in Japan
